scalesUsed.notes: E - G - A - Bb - B - D
scalesUsed.application: The core framework for Hendrix's iconic bluesy solo, double-stops, and intro turnaround lick
Blended into Hendrix's rhythm fills for sweet, soulful major-third color

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: E blues-rock tonality built over the famous reverse Circle of Fifths chord sequence (C - G - D - A - E)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor is the relative minor of E major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: The reverse Circle of Fifths progression: each chord resolves up a fourth (or down a fifth) until reaching the triumphant E major tonic.
mainProgression.description: The reverse Circle of Fifths progression: each chord resolves up a fourth (or down a fifth) until reaching the triumphant E major tonic.

sectionProgressions.progression: E - F# - G - G# - A - Bb - B - E
sectionProgressions.description: High string double-stops moving into a low chromatic walking bassline resolving to E7#9
The cyclical 5-chord progression played with Hendrix-style thumb-over chord embellishments
Slow-burn E minor pentatonic blues solo targeting roots and minor thirds with heavy vibrato

harmonicFunction: C (♭VI) - Borrowed submediant establishing the starting point of the fifths cascade
G (♭III) - Resolves down a fifth from C, providing major-pentatonic rock drive
D (♭VII) - Subtonic chord providing classic rock Mixolydian color
A (IV) - Subdominant leading directly into the tonic
E (I) - Satisfying home tonic resolution that sustains with epic rock authority

techniques.name: Reverse Circle of Fifths & Hendrix Thumb Fretting
techniques.description: Using the fretting thumb to anchor the low root notes while index and ring fingers decorate the triads with double-stops and hammer-ons

notes: Intro double-stop sliding on strings 1 and 2
Chromatic bass run: 0-1-2-3-4 on low E, moving to A string
sequence: Play the sliding high E/B string double stop intro
Execute the chromatic bass walkup leading into E7#9
Cycle C → G → D → A → E with rhythmic thumb pulses and hammer-on fills
Solo in E minor pentatonic in the 12th position
tips: Relax your fretting wrist so your thumb can wrap comfortably over the top of the neck
Use a neck single-coil pickup with volume rolled back slightly for sweet cleans
Dig in with dynamic pick attack during the solo to push the tube amp into natural overdrive

sections.name: Intro Double-Stops & Walkup
sections.description: Hendrix's historic opening statement with high string slides and low chromatic walkup.
notes: Slide high notes with ring and middle fingers
Clean thumb bass walkup from open E to 4th fret G#
Stab the final E chord with authority

sections.name: Circle of Fifths Progression
sections.description: The famous C - G - D - A - E progression played with rhythmic feel and hammer-on fills.
notes: Accent the root notes on the beat
Let the final E chord ring for a full measure

sections.name: Blues Guitar Solo
sections.description: One of the most expressive blues-rock solos in history, full of singing bends and wide vibrato.
notes: Target the 15th-fret B string full bend to high E
Use your index finger to mute non-played strings
Wring out wide, emotive vibrato at the top of bends

guitar.pickup: Neck single-coil pickup for rhythm; Middle/Bridge single-coil for solo

effects.distortion: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (Germanium or Silicon)
effects.other: Coiled guitar cable for high-frequency roll-off

beginner.title: The 5-Chord Sequence
steps: Memorize the order of the five chords: C, G, D, A, and E
Practice shifting between each chord in half notes at 70 BPM
Hold the final E major chord for two full bars

intermediate.title: Intro Lick & Bass Walkup
steps: Learn the high sliding double-stop intro
Master the chromatic low bass walkup into the E chord
Play the entire song at 84 BPM with steady rhythm

advanced.title: Solo & Hendrix Embellishments
steps: Master the 12th-position E minor pentatonic solo note-for-note
Add thumb-over bass fret techniques and hammer-on chord fills
Control fuzz and volume dynamics using your guitar volume knob

commonMistakes: Bending out of tune on the 15th fret B string in the solo
Rushing the relaxed, heavy 84 BPM tempo
Forgetting the chromatic passing notes in the intro walkup
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Fifths chord sequence shifting (C → G → D → A → E)
5 minutes: Intro lick and chromatic walkup with metronome
metronomeWork: Practice the chord changes at 65 BPM, then increase to 84 BPM
Work on solo phrasing with metronome clicks on 2 and 4
